statement: For every finite set X, permutation δ:X→X with a_j cycles of length j, and integer m≥0, the number of δ-invariant subsets U⊆X with |U|=m equals [x^m]∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j)^{a_j}.
proof: Decompose X into its disjoint δ-orbits, which are exactly the cycles. If U is δ-invariant, then for every u∈U all iterates δ^k(u) lie in U, so the entire cycle containing u lies in U. Thus U is a union of cycles. Conversely every union of cycles is δ-invariant. For each length-j cycle, choosing it contributes x^j to the size-generating polynomial if included and 1 if excluded. Choices for distinct cycles are independent, so multiplying these factors gives a polynomial whose coefficient of x^m counts exactly the invariant unions of size m. Grouping equal-length cycles yields ∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j)^{a_j}.

statement: Let δ act on X with a_j cycles of length j, and C act on Y with c_j cycles of length j. The number of injective maps ψ:X→Y satisfying C∘ψ=ψ∘δ is ∏_{j≥1}(c_j)_{a_j} j^{a_j}, where (c)_a=c(c−1)…(c−a+1), interpreted as zero if a>c.
proof: If Cψ=ψδ, then for x on a δ-cycle of length j, C^jψ(x)=ψ(δ^j x)=ψ(x); injectivity implies the least positive C-period of ψ(x) is exactly j. Thus ψ maps each δ-cycle to a C-cycle of the same length. Distinct δ-cycles map to distinct C-cycles, since their images would otherwise overlap, contradicting injectivity. For each j, assign the a_j distinguishable δ-cycles injectively to ambient cycles in (c_j)_{a_j} ways. For each assignment, choose the image of a fixed representative on each δ-cycle in j ways; equivariance then determines the rest. The choices are independent. Conversely, every such assignment and phase choice defines an injective equivariant map. Multiplying gives the formula.

statement: Let X,Y be finite sets with |X|=m and |Y|=N≥m, and let δ be any permutation of X. Then Σ_{C∈Sym(Y)} |{ψ:X↪Y : C∘ψ=ψ∘δ}| = N!.
proof: Count pairs (C,ψ) satisfying the equation by first choosing ψ. There are (N)_m injections. For each ψ, the equation forces C(ψ(x))=ψ(δ(x)) for every x∈X, specifying C on ψ(X). The remaining N−m points can be permuted in (N−m)! ways. Thus the pair count is (N)_m(N−m)!=N!. This counts the same pairs as summing, over each C∈Sym(Y), its compatible injections ψ, proving the identity.
